newsitem.title: FINLAND: ASPO SEES IMPROVING 1997 PROFIT, SALES.
newsitem.headline: ASPO SEES IMPROVING 1997 PROFIT, SALES.

text.p: Finnish chemicals, electronic components and steel processing group Aspoyhtyma Oy said on Thursday it expected profits and net sales to improve this year.
"The group's net sales and profits are expected to improve in 1997," Aspo said in a statement with its 1996 results.

Aspoyhtyma confirmed its 1996 profit before extraordinary items and tax was 65.5 million markka, down from 97.6 million in 1995. Its 1996 net sales were 1,109.7 million markka, down from 1,059.1 million.
"Growth in the electronics division is expected to continue due to healthy industry demand and efficient overall capacity utilisation," Aspo said.
"However, increasing price competition may have a negative impact on electronics earnings and forecasting must have a short-term horizon because of the volatility of this sector," the company said.
"The financial performance of the chemicals division will depend on developments in Russia and chemical prices in Finland," it said.
"Prospects for the shipping division look reasonably good," it said.
